question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let $u=7-4x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u$, solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{7-4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-4x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x real; x != 7/4; antiderivative on each connected interval
